messages:
kyle: Heads up — CI started failing on runtime-kernel branch after I added support for sm_89 gencode. nvcc exits with 'Unsupported gpu architecture' in the fatbin step. build log: https://ci.internal/builds/5423

nina: Which CUDA toolkit image is the runner using? I saw weird mismatches yesterday on ubuntu-22 images.

kyle: CI image shows CUDA 12.1 in /usr/local/cuda; I was targeting 12.2 locally. Error snippet: `nvcc fatal : Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_89'`

frank: Sounds like a toolchain mismatch. If the runner's nvcc is older it won't accept compute_89. Quick checks: `nvcc --version` and `cuobjdump --version` in the container. Also check driver vs toolkit compatibility.

ci-bot: Build #5423 failed: https://ci.internal/builds/5423 — nvcc exit code 2 (artifact attached)

kyle: Our current CMake uses flags like `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80` plus `-arch=sm_86` for fallbacks. Adding sm_89 naively made CMake append `-gencode=arch=compute_89,code=sm_89` which triggers on older nvcc.

nina: Also note adding multiple `-gencode` targets increases fatbin size a lot. With sm_80+sm_86+sm_89 I'm seeing ~+45% for libkernels.so locally. That's a regression we can't ship.

frank: Tradeoffs: include PTX for the newest arch(s) and only emit SASS for older SMs to keep binary size lower. Example pattern: `-gencode=arch=compute_89,code=ptx` and `-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86` and `-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80`. Newer drivers will JIT PTX; older ones will use provided SASS.

kyle: That follows our RFC about PTX fallbacks. We should be careful about PTX/ptxas versions — nvcc may emit PTX targeting a specific ptx version. Suggest adding `-Xptxas=-v` in CI to log register usage and `--generate-code` style flags in CMake. Minimal example in CMake: `add_compile_options("-gencode=arch=compute_89,code=ptx" "-gencode=arch=compute_86,code=sm_86" "-gencode=arch=compute_80,code=sm_80")`

nina: Add `-Xptxas=-v` yes — helps see register pressure. Also `--fatbin` and `cuobjdump --dump-ptx` are helpful to verify presence of PTX sections.

frank: Longer term: we can split kernel artifacts per-arch and choose which .so to load at startup. Big refactor but reduces per-binary size for Dedicated/RP customers. For now PTX strategy is lower risk.

kyle: Immediate plan: update CMake to emit PTX for compute_89 and SASS for sm_86/sm_80 only. Also flip CI to run matrix jobs: CUDA 12.1 and 12.2 runners so we catch toolchain mismatches early.

ci-bot: @kyle opened MR #1809: "ci: gencode PTX for sm_89, add cuda-12.2 runner, size smoke" — https://ci.internal/mr/1809

nina: Please add a small CI smoke step that runs `cuobjdump --dump-ptx libkernels.so` and records whether PTX for compute_89 exists, and also capture `du -h` on the artifact so we can detect size regressions. We should enforce a soft threshold (warn) and a hard threshold (fail) for size.

kyle: Will add a script `tools/ci/check_kernel_artifacts.py` that fails if libkernels.so > 80MB or if PTX for compute_89 is missing. I'll gate the size failure on a nightly job first, then enforce on PRs if stable.

frank: Also add a short note in the RFC follow-up about driver compatibility and fallback policy for Private deployments — some customers won't have drivers that JIT new PTX.

nina: Agreed. Document supported compute capabilities per deployment mode and provide a knob in runtime to prefer SASS-only or PTX-inclusive builds.

kyle: Made the changes in MR #1809 and added the smoke job. Merged to main — I'll watch the nightly size metric. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
